content: The extension for the IT service desk is 2210 [1][3].
Full-time staff get 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays [1]. Up to 5 unused days may be carried over to 31 March [1].
To request Ledgerline access, you must use form NBC-F-031, signed by your line manager [1].

For lithium batteries, use Moorland Logistics service code **DGX** (Dangerous goods / lithium batteries, UK and EU road) [3][4]. Parcels containing a battery pack must be booked under service DGX, as carrier drivers will reject consignments if the manifest service code does not match the parcel's hazardous markings [1][2][3].
Voltway Cells' current supplier code is VC-EIN-0042 [1][2]. Its former code, VC-EIN-0009, is blocked and renamed "(old code, do not use)" [1][2][5].
Voltway's lead time for battery packs is six weeks from order [1].

No, you cannot order from Brightcell Energy today [2]. 

Under Purchase Policy 6.2 (as amended by AMD-SUP-2026-02), lithium-cell parts require a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file and checked before the first order, which must be less than 12 months old and valid for at least 60 days after the order [2]. Brightcell's UN 38.3 report is currently being renewed and is not expected until December 2026, so they cannot pass [1][2]. Additionally, under Policy 6.4, a cheaper quote alone is not a valid reason to switch suppliers for a lithium-cell part [2]. Brightcell is also not yet set up in the supplier master [4].

Luis Moreno instructed to send Brightcell the onboarding pack and continue ordering from Voltway for the launch [2]. Note that Ledgerline’s certificate check is switched off, so a clean Save does not permit the purchase [2].

**Meaning:**
`ERR-PO-0412` indicates that the tax code does not match the supplier's country [1][4][5]. The revised error message displays `TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY` followed by the supplier's country code in brackets [4][5]. This typically happens because Fetch automatically defaults to `VAT20-UK`, even for overseas suppliers [4].

**How to fix it:**
1. Check the supplier country code shown in brackets at the end of the message [3][4][5].
2. Amend the tax code on the order line:
   - Outside the UK: enter `VAT20-RC` (or `VAT5-RC` for reduced-rate items) [3][4].
   - UK supplier: enter `VAT20-UK` [3][4].
   - Check each line item individually on split or mixed orders [3].
3. Ensure the cursor remains in the line details area and press **F8** again to save and validate the change [2][4].

A battery pack shipped on its own is sent as UN3480 (lithium-ion batteries) [1]. In addition, any separate pack travelling in its own carton requires UN3480 documentation, even if consigned on the same pallet as a complete bicycle [2].
The letter template used to ask a supplier for a new UN 38.3 test report when a certificate is expiring within 90 days is NBC-L-07 [1].
The battery handling course is BHT-01 (Battery handling) [1][2][3]. It must be repeated every 24 months [1][2][3].
The nightly backup (JOB-SYS-001) runs daily at 01:30 [1][3]. During this routine, Ledgerline is in a read-only state from 01:30 to 01:50 [1][3].
R. Ainsworth, Managing Director, signed the Ledgerline licence agreement for Northbridge Cycles Ltd on 14 August 1998 [1].

The paper copy for PO/2026/00452 records approval by Daniel Okafor on 06/04/2026 [1]. It also notes that system approval is recorded in Ledgerline [1], where Ledgerline records approval by KMENSAH [2].
The standard working week is 37.5 hours, Monday to Friday [1][2].
Voltway's rates are delivered (DAP Manchester) [1]. You must never add a freight line or a freight charge to a Voltway order, and if their invoice shows freight, it must be sent back [1].
Voltway Cells' VAT number is NL859312774B01 [2][3].
The purchasing bot pilot interface (INT-007) has no owner (listed as "(none)") [1], and its associated integration account, SVC_AGENT, has no named owner [2].
NOT IN THE DOCUMENTS. The specific supplier code or document reference for the ISO 9001 certificate is not specified.

A sales order must be confirmed by 15:30 to be picked the same day and delivered the next working day in the UK [1]. If an order is confirmed after this daily cut-off, the warehouse does not pick the goods that day [2].
According to the 2023 count sheet for Aisle B, the items were counted by A. Tanaka and checked by C. Shaw [1].
Nordic Cell's new UN 38.3 test report is expected in late November 2026 [1].

To onboard a new supplier under the current policy [2]:

1. **Proposal:** As a purchase executive, propose the supplier with at least one written quotation and the reason an existing supplier cannot meet the need [2].
2. **Collect documents:** Before creation in Ledgerline, collect the VAT registration certificate (VAT number), company registration number, a bank letter confirming the account, proof of insurance, and the signed Supplier Code of Conduct [2].
3. **Check duplicates:** Search the supplier master on screen `PUR-SUP-03` by name, city, and VAT number, and attach the search result to the onboarding file [2].
4. **Approval & Creation:** Submit the onboarding file to the purchase manager for approval [2]. Only after approval may you create the supplier in Ledgerline using screen `PUR-SUP-01` [2]. 

A new supplier must be fully onboarded under POL-SUP-003 before any order can be placed [4].
NOT IN THE DOCUMENTS. The sources state that e-mails should be kept on the order file for audit purposes, but they do not state an e-mail retention period [1][5].

To rescue an order stuck in Draft due to a closed cost centre (warning W-CC-114) [2][5]:

1. Open the order on screen PUR-POM-06 and press Fetch [2].
2. Amend the cost centre to an open cost centre [1][2][5].

Once amended, the order status changes to AP or PA according to the normal rules [1][2], and it can be released once approved [1].

To upload a supplier certificate, use the Certificates tab of the supplier via service `sup_cert_upload` (module PUR) [2][4]. 

Submit the following required fields [1][3]:
- Supplier code (`sup_cd`) [1]
- Certificate type (`cert_type`, e.g. UN38.3) [1][2][5]
- Document reference (`doc_ref`), matching the header on the scanned paperwork [1][3][5]
- Valid-to date (`valid_to`) [1][3][5]

Attach the scanned test report with the upload [2].

Do not press Save again, as doing so creates a second order [1]. 

Wait one minute, then search for the order via Purchase, Order list by supplier, item, and today's date, or by client reference [1]. If the order exists, the Save worked and you may continue from it [1].

To cancel a purchase order, press Cancel and enter a reason [1][3]. This sets the order status to CN, releases the committed budget, and removes the quantity from stock on order for a released order [3]. Before cancelling, check the receipt status; if a delivery note has already been processed against a line, it cannot simply be cancelled and must be cleared through the standard returns routine [5].

Ledgerline does not send a cancellation notice [1][3]. You must e-mail the supplier yourself on the same day and keep the e-mail on the order file [1].

To receive goods against an order:

1. Check the supplier's delivery note against the purchase order (PO) number [1]. The order must be released (RL), or Ledgerline halts with `ERR-GRN-0102` [1].
2. Physically count the delivery against the delivery note and PO lines before keying figures, taking care not to mistake outer cartons for individual pieces [2][4].
3. On screen **INV-GRN-03**, enter the PO number and press **Fetch** [1].
4. Enter the quantity received against each line [1][2]. You cannot exceed the order balance (`ERR-GRN-0204`) [1][3]. 
5. Receive lithium-cell parts into warehouse **WH-MAN-QC** [1][5]. (Refuse damaged battery packaging, photograph it, and report it to Quality [1]).
6. Enter the supplier’s delivery note number and any visible carrier damage in **Remarks** [1][2].
7. Press **Save** (or **F8 Save**) [1][2]. Each partial delivery requires its own GRN [1][2][3].

When a UN 38.3 certificate is about to expire:

- On the first working day of each month, the senior buyer runs the certificate-expiry report (job JOB-PUR-022) with a 90-day window [1] (also referenced under MAN-PUR-72 §22.6 [3]).
- For certificates expiring within 90 days, write to the supplier using letter template NBC-L-07 requesting a new test report [1].
- If no new report arrives by 60 days before expiry, send a second reminder and notify the purchase manager [1]. Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, no new orders may be raised once fewer than 60 days remain [1].
- Upon expiry, e-mail all buyers with the subject `CERT EXPIRED - DO NOT ORDER` along with the supplier's name and code [1].
- When renewed, upload the certificate as a new row in Ledgerline ERP; never overwrite the old record [1][4].

NOT IN THE DOCUMENTS. The provided sources do not specify the scheduled date or timing for the annual stock count, only noting an archived 2016 mention of it occurring before the financial year closes [2] and a past count sheet dated 25 March 2023 [1].

If a battery pack is dropped:

- Leave it stationary, clear the gangway, and fetch the shift fire warden immediately [1].
- Take it out of use and isolate it immediately, regardless of external appearance; never return it to regular stock or leave it on workbenches [2][3][5].
- Operators must halt work, raise the physical quarantine flag, apply the initial warning label, and notify the line supervisor without leaving the area unattended [4].
- The line supervisor must arrange safe physical transfer to the designated outdoor fire-rated quarantine locker using a heavy-duty transit container and protective gloves, without attempting to test, charge, or dismantle it [4]. 
- If treated as compromised, it must be placed into the designated red bin in fire cell BAT-Z4 and covered with vermiculite, rather than put in standard scrap cages [5]. Do not book it to scrap before quality inspection [3].

To raise a purchase request in Ledgerline ERP 7.2:

1. Open screen **PUR-PR-01** [3].
2. Enter the item code and press **F3** (Fetch) [3]. Ledgerline automatically populates the unit, warehouse, your default cost centre, and an estimated rate based on the last released order [3].
3. Check the cost centre on screen **FIN-CC-01** before saving, as Finance may have closed your default cost centre and Ledgerline does not display a warning [3].
4. Press **F8** to save the request, which sets the status to **DR** [3].
5. Press **F9** to submit [3]. If the request is within your approval limit, it is approved immediately; if it exceeds your limit, it routes to your manager [3].

Never amend bank details based on an e-mail alone [2][3]. You must perform an independent check:

1. Obtain the supplier’s telephone number from the established ledger record or the separate agreed supplier contacts list—never from the incoming correspondence, e-mail footer, letterhead, or website [1][2].
2. Call the supplier with two AP staff members on the line and speak directly to a known contact to confirm the change originated from them [1][2].
3. Ask the contact to verbally confirm both the existing and new account details [1].
4. Record the call on screen AP-BNK-06 (service `bnk_verify`) and retain call details alongside the written request [1][2] (warning `W-BNK-120` holds payments until recorded) [2].
5. If you cannot reach the contact or they seem unsure, place the account on temporary hold and alert Marta Kowalski immediately [1]. Submit for approval only once verification is complete [1].

A damaged-pack incident is reported through the following steps:

- Report the incident to Quality within the same shift by submitting a non-conformance report on screen QA-NCR-02 [1].
- The storekeeper raises a quarantine movement entry in Ledgerline ERP to transfer the pack's serial number out of free stock into the designated holding location [2].
- Complete a physical quarantine tie-on card by hand and attach it to the fireproof container holding the pack [2].
- Immediately update the quarantine register kept in the battery store with the pack serial number, reporting department, apparent defect, and the handler's initials [2].

Under current procedure SOP-PUR-002 v1.4, once your purchase request is approved (status AP):

1. Raise the order on screen PUR-PO-01 [4].
2. Set the order type to STD [4].
3. Enter the request number in the Source PR field [4].
4. Enter the supplier and the item, then press F3 (Fetch) [4]. 

Note that under the superseded v1.3 procedure, pressing Fetch was optional [3]; under v1.4, you must press F3 (Fetch) after entering the supplier and item [4].

To submit a travel expense claim under current policy POL-TEX-007 v2.4:

1. Obtain prior verbal approval for travel from your department head [2].
2. Log into the legacy system and access screen AP-EXP-09 to generate an expense header [5].
3. Enter each line item individually with its business purpose, cost centre, and ledger allocation [5]. Do not conflate mileage and public transport costs into one line [2].
4. Collate and reference all paper receipts (detailed VAT receipts for lines over £10) to the system line items [2][5].
5. Verify that the screen AP-EXP-09 total matches the paper total [2].
6. Submit the physical receipts alongside the electronic batch to your line manager for review and system approval [3][5]. Once approved, it routes to the purchase ledger clerk for payment [5].

Note: POL-TEX-007 v3.0 comes into force on 1 January 2027, requiring submission within 45 days [1].

Before starting, staff complete invoice and credit note registrations across Manchester and Leeds, clear query holds, verify bank balances, check communication software, and ensure no conflicting open proposals exist [4]. Proposal job JOB-AP-030 runs against records [5].

Operators locate runs using PAYMENT RUN LIST [2]. If adjustments are required before approval or release, click `pay_cancel` (PAYMENT RUN CANCEL) and enter a REASON [2].

Once reviewed, submit the batch using `pay_approve` (PAYMENT RUN APPROVE); missing rights trigger ERR-APR-0003, and self-approval triggers ERR-PAY-0430 [1][5]. 

Once approved, click `pay_release` to execute PAYMENT RUN RELEASE [1]. Next, press `pay_file` (PAYMENT RUN FILE) to produce the bank transmission batch [1].

Finally, staff file the signed authorisation sheet, proposal report, payment summary, and printed bank transmission confirmation chronologically by payment date [3].

To return faulty goods to a supplier:

1. **Prerequisites**: Return goods within 30 days of receipt [1]. Check the line’s billing status on the purchase order inquiry screen; if the invoice has posted, screen INV-RTV-07 will halt with ERR-RTV-0230, requiring the quarantine docket to go to purchase ledger for an AP-DBN-04 entry [2].
2. **Preparation**: Locate the original GRN NO, ensure quality control has signed off the non-conformance report (NCR NO), confirm the goods receipt is not cancelled/reversed, and verify physical stock is segregated and labelled in quarantine [4][5].
3. **Supplier & Transport**: Purchasing must agree credit or replacement with the supplier and schedule transport with an approved carrier [3][4].
4. **System Processing & Dispatch**: Process the return on screen INV-RTV-07 to transfer stock out of active inventory [1][5]. Ensure dispatch paperwork accompanies the freight and file the carrier's signed collection manifest with the RTV or debit note paperwork [2][5].

Before booking a parcel with a battery pack, check the following:

- **Despatch note and contents:** Check the despatch note against the carton contents to apply the `PKG-LBL-UN` label with the correct designation: `UN3480` if the lithium battery pack travels alone as a replacement part, or `UN3481` if installed in the frame or boxed with the bicycle (never apply both) [1]. 
- **Label printing:** Ensure the lithium battery label is printed before despatch is posted (to avoid `ERR-DLV-0320`) [3].
- **Carrier service code:** When booking on `SAL-FRT-12`, ensure the consignment is booked under dangerous-goods service code `DGX` with Moorland Logistics so the manifest matches the parcel’s hazardous markings [1][3][4].
- **Returns verification:** If processing returns on screen, verify the record indicates the specialized dangerous-goods carrier before providing final return instructions [5].

To change the supplier, you cannot amend the existing order; you must cancel it and raise a new order [1]. On PUR-POM-06, you can only change the quantity, need-by date, or cost centre [1][3].

To cancel the order:
1. Open the order on PUR-POM-06, press Cancel, and enter a reason [1].
2. E-mail the supplier yourself the same day, as Ledgerline sends no cancellation notice [1].
3. Keep the e-mail on the order file [1].

After cancelling, raise a new order for the intended supplier [1]. Note that orders in CN, RJ, or CL status cannot be amended (ERR-PO-0801) [1].

Yes. A supplier of chargers (classified as a lithium-cell part) must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate on file in Ledgerline [1][4]. Chargers may only be purchased from a supplier holding this certificate, which must be uploaded and checked before the first order is placed [1][4].

Kitting teams call off battery packs from fire-resistant storage cages for the production line [1]. Workshop technicians must draw batteries only against issued build kits [4]. 

Because battery packs require individual serial tracking, they do not clear through the standard backflush routine [2]. Instead, operators must book the serial numbers through the manual material screen [2]. Any surplus or unassigned packs must be returned to stores before the end of the shift [4].

When approving an order for a lithium-cell part (a BAT-, MTR-, or CHG- item, or anything with the lithium-cell flag), the approver must write `CERT OK` followed by the certificate's document reference in the approval comment [1][2]. 

For example: `CERT OK UN38.3-TR/VC/2026/118` [1]. 

Without this comment, the order cannot be approved [1], and leaving it blank causes delays in the goods inward bay [2].

In force today (26 October 2026), a direct purchase order without a purchase request is permitted only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less [1][3][4]. 

Under Amendment AMD-PUR-2026-03, this limit will reduce to £25,000 or less gross, including VAT, effective from 1 December 2026 [1][3]. IT will update the setting in Ledgerline on the evening of 30 November 2026 [3].
Approval limits apply to the gross value including VAT, not the basic value [1][3][4].

To put battery cartons away:

- Move packs only in their cartons on a pallet, stacked no more than four cartons high [1].
- Put packs away only in fire cells BAT-Z1 to BAT-Z4 [1].
- Check the cell's count board first; each cell must hold no more than 1,500 packs [1]. If adding the pallet breaches allowable quantities or physical cartons exceed the board tally, halt movement, leave the pallet in the transit lane, and notify the stores supervisor [3].
- Do not place any carton in the fire cells if it shows impact, crushing, dampness, or has been dropped; move it immediately to the quarantine holding area, apply a red physical tag, and record the movement in the system [1][3].
- If a carton lacks a legible date label, keep it on the inbound staging pallet and request a reprint from the inventory clerk [3].

No, you cannot approve an order you raised [4]. 

Under company policy, nobody may approve an order they raised [4]. In Ledgerline ERP (screen PUR-POA-04), you cannot approve an order you created; attempting to do so will result in error ERR-APR-0003 [5].

No. Splitting one requirement into several orders to stay inside a limit is not allowed [1]. 

Orders for the same item from the same supplier raised within seven days of each other are treated as one requirement [1].

Yes, it is allowed [1][2]. 

Under current policy POL-PUR-001 v4.1, you must enter the rate agreed in the current rate contract [1][2]. Any order raised at a rate more than 2% above the contract rate requires you to record your manager's written reason or justification in the order remarks [1][2]. 

(Note that the previous threshold of more than 5% under POL-PUR-001 v4.0 has been superseded [3].)

You must not inform the requester that an order has been placed until the order has its official document number assigned by Ledgerline and has reached Released status [1][3]. 

You must never make informal commitments while an order is pending or in Draft status [1]. Telling the requester their order has gone through when the document sits in approved status is a regular error; the purchase order has not been transmitted until it passes through the release screen and shows released status [4].

No. Under current policy, an expired certificate counts as no certificate [2][5]. 

The supplier remains ACTIVE in the supplier master, but no lithium-cell part may be ordered from it until a new certificate is uploaded and checked [2].

Yes. Approval of a purchase request covers the purchase order raised from it, provided the approver's personal limit is high enough to cover the final order's gross value (including VAT) [1][2]. 

If the final gross value increases beyond that original approver's limit, a higher-level approval must be obtained [1].

No. Integration and service accounts (role SYS-ADMIN, such as SVC_AGENT) have no approval authority under the approval matrix, regardless of their technical permissions in Ledgerline [3]. A service account never approves documents [2]. 

Any document approved by a service account is treated as unapproved and must be cancelled or re-approved by a person [3].

Above £5,000,000, the order requires the Managing Director's written approval outside Ledgerline [1][2]. 

For such an order, Ledgerline displays error code ERR-APR-0009 (no approver found), and the plant head's office records the Managing Director's approval in the system [1].

Under current policy POL-SUP-003 v2.3:

* **VAT number:** The VAT number is the test of sameness; two records with the same VAT number are the same supplier, and one legal supplier has exactly one active code [2]. Ledgerline blocks creating a second supplier with an already registered VAT number (ERR-SUP-0118) [2].
* **Name and city match:** A name that is close to an existing supplier in the same city must be treated as that supplier until shown otherwise [2]. 
* **Different city or VAT number:** A near-match in a different city or with a different VAT number is a different supplier [2].

An overseas supplier gets the reverse charge tax code **VAT20-RC** [1][3][4][5]. More generally, overseas suppliers require an `-RC` code [2], which also includes **VAT5-RC** for a 5% reverse charge rate [5]. 

When entering an overseas order, Ledgerline defaults to the domestic code `VAT20-UK`, which must be manually changed to `VAT20-RC` to avoid error `ERR-PO-0412` [1][2][3][4].

Any gift worth more than £50 from a supplier or customer must be declared in the gifts register within five working days [1]. If you cannot determine the exact value, you must treat it as exceeding £50 and submit the declaration [3]. 

In addition, all gifts or offers of hospitality must be declared through line management before acceptance (or immediately following receipt if advance notice was impossible) [2]. 

Note that as purchase staff, you must not accept any gift, regardless of value, from a supplier taking part in an open quotation or tender [1][4].
Battery packs are kept at a state of charge between 30% and 50% while in store [1][2][4]. Packs below 30% or above 50% state of charge are rejected during inspection [5].
One fire cell can hold no more than 1,500 packs [1][2][3][4][5].

A new requirement above £100,000 gross requires three written quotations, which must be compared on form NBC-F-118 [1]. If only two quotations can be obtained for a requirement above this limit, you must refer the matter immediately to the purchasing manager and obtain written dispensation before proceeding [2]. 

Items covered by a current rate contract require no quotation [1]. Additionally, initiating an onboarding request for a new vendor requires at least one written quotation [4]. 

The sources do not state the quotation requirements for new purchases of £100,000 gross or below.
Frames carry a 5-year warranty [1][2]. Battery packs carry a 2-year warranty from the date of sale to the rider [1][2].

Yes, you can [1][2]. 

Under company policy, an approver on leave may delegate in writing to someone of the same or a higher role for a stated period [1]. In daily operational practice, the transfer must be arranged prior to departure, and internal audit requires delegations to remain within equivalent operational tiers, such as peers within the purchasing department [2]. Because another purchase executive holds the same role, delegating to them is permitted [1][2]. Delegation to a lower role is not allowed [1].

No. A battery pack returned under warranty is never put back into stock, and regardless of test results, no returned pack may re-enter general stock [1][2][3]. 

Instead, the warehouse team must quarantine the pack immediately upon receipt and transfer the cost directly to battery refurbishment (cost centre PRD-09), or route it for recycling [1][2].
Incoming lithium-cell parts are inspected at acceptable quality level (AQL) 0.65 [1][2].

No. Although a supplier created in Ledgerline is ACTIVE from the day it is created, no order may be placed with it until every document in §3.2 and, for lithium-cell parts, the certificate in §4 is on file [2][3].
`po_fetch` always returns `VAT20-UK` as the tax code (`tax_cd`), regardless of the supplier's country [1][2][5].
Supplier certificates (UN 38.3, ISO) are kept for 10 years after the supplier is blocked [1]. Their record owner is Purchase [1].

Today, the meal allowance on an overnight trip is £35 a day, with receipts [1]. It covers an evening meal and refreshments [4]. 

Under POL-TEX-007 v3.0, which comes into force on 1 January 2027, this allowance will increase to £40 a day [2][3].

The `sup_cert_upload` service requires the following mandatory fields:

- `sup_cd` (str, SUP CD) [1][4]
- `cert_type` (str, CERT TYPE) [1][4]
- `doc_ref` (str, DOC REF) [1][4]
- `valid_to` (date, VALID TO) [1][4]

There are no optional fields [1].

The `sup_create` service takes the following fields [1][2]:

**Required fields:**
* `name` (SUP NAME, type `str`) [1][2]
* `city` (CITY, type `str`) [1][2]
* `state` (COUNTRY CD (2), type `str`) [1][2]

**Optional fields:**
* `vat_no` (VAT number, type `str`) [1][2]
* `pt_cd` (PAY TERM CD, type `str`) [1][2]

The mandatory fields for `po_save` are:

- `sup_cd` [1][2][3]
- `itm_cd` [1][2][3]
- `qty` [1][2][3]
- `rate` [1][2][3]
- `tax_cd` [1][2][3]
- `cc_cd` [1][2][3]
- `need_dt` [1][3]

Per Release Note RN-7.2.3, `fetch_tok` (returned by calling `po_fetch`) is now also mandatory in the payload, changing its previous optional status [3][5]. 

Additionally, `pr_no` is mandatory when creating a standard PO (`STD`) [1].
The service `po_release` belongs to screen PUR-POR-05 (PURCHASE ORDER RELEASE) [1][3][4].

The estimated value (`est_value`) is computed as:

`qty` × `est_rate` × 1.20 (quantity × estimated rate × 1.20) [1][2][4]. 

Ledgerline assumes 20% VAT on every request, regardless of the item's actual tax [1][2].

Under service `grn_save` (GOODS RECEIPT SAVE), the request fields are:

**Required (Mandatory):**
* `po_no` (type: str) – PO NO [1][4]
* `qty` (type: int) – QTY RECD [1][4]

**Optional:**
* `whs_cd` (type: str) – WHS CD [1][4]
* `remarks` (type: str) – REMARKS [1][4]

`fetch_tok` is a token returned by the Fetch service (`po_fetch`) and required by Save (`po_save`) [1][3][4]. It is valid once, for one supplier and item [1][2]. Interface routines must call `po_fetch` before executing `po_save` to pass `fetch_tok` in the payload [4]. In the database table `fetch_tok`, its fields include `screen`, `ctx`, `created_on`, and `used` [5].

According to the `po_save` specification, the service can return the following errors:

**Service Errors:**
- `ERR-SCR-0221` FETCH NOT DONE [2][3]
- `ERR-SUP-0030` SUPPLIER NOT FOUND [2][3]
- `ERR-SUP-0031` SUPPLIER NOT ACTIVE [2]
- `ERR-ITM-0011` ITEM NOT FOUND OR INACTIVE [2]
- `ERR-PO-0201` QTY MUST BE > 0 [2]
- `ERR-PO-0105` NEED DATE IN PAST [2]
- `ERR-PO-0602` SOURCE PR MANDATORY FOR STD PO [2]
- `ERR-PO-0603` SOURCE PR NOT APPROVED (<status>) [2]
- `ERR-PO-0604` ITEM/QTY NOT AS PER PR [1][2]
- `ERR-PO-0611` DIR PO CANNOT REFER PR [1][5]
- `ERR-PO-0610` DIRECT PO LIMIT 50000 EXCEEDED, RAISE PR [1][5]
- `ERR-TAX-0101` INVALID TAX CODE [1][5]
- `ERR-PO-0412` TAX CODE DOES NOT MATCH SUPPLIER COUNTRY (<state>) [1][5]
- `ERR-CC-0009` COST CENTRE NOT FOUND [1][5]
- `ERR-BUD-0207` BUDGET EXCEEDED FOR <cc_cd> [1][5]
- `ERR-APR-0009` NO APPROVER FOUND [1][5]

**Common Errors:**
- `ERR-SEC-0001` ACCESS DENIED [4][5]
- `ERR-SYS-0421` <FIELD> MANDATORY [4]
- `ERR-SYS-0422` UNKNOWN FIELD <FIELD> / BAD VALUE FOR <FIELD> [4]
- `ERR-SYS-0503` SERVER BUSY, TRY LATER [4]

In Ledgerline ERP 7.2, the `state` field of a supplier represents the two-letter country code (described in the database as "Two-letter country code (1998 name)" and on screen/service definitions as "COUNTRY CD (2)") [3][4].
The service `sup_create` uses screen **PUR-SUP-01** (SUPPLIER MASTER CREATE) [1][2][3][4].

**ERR-SCR-0221 (FETCH NOT DONE)** means that an order was saved without running Fetch (pressing F3) for the current supplier and item, or after changing them [1][2][3]. Ledgerline rejects the save because background linkages are missing until F3 is pressed [4].

To resolve it, press **F3** (Fetch), verify the fetched values, and save the order again [2][3].

**ERR-SUP-0031** means "Supplier not active" [3] (or "SUPPLIER NOT ACTIVE" [5]). 

It is caused when an order cannot be saved because the supplier status is BLOCKED [2][3][5]. Orders can only be saved for ACTIVE suppliers [2]. 

To resolve it, use the supplier's active code; a blocked old code usually has a replacement [3][5].

**ERR-SUP-0118** means **VAT NO ALREADY REGISTERED** (or "VAT number already registered") [1][2][3]. 

**Cause:** A supplier with this VAT number already exists in Ledgerline [1][3]. Ledgerline raises this error (via service `sup_create`) and refuses to create a second supplier record with an already registered VAT number [2][3][4].

**Remedy:** Search for the supplier and use the existing code; do not create a second record [1][3].

**ERR-PO-0610** means “DIRECT PO LIMIT 50000 EXCEEDED, RAISE PR” [2] (or “Direct PO limit exceeded, raise PR” [3]). 

It indicates that a direct (DIR) order’s gross value exceeds the configured direct-order limit (shipped default £50,000) upon saving (raised by `po_save`) [1][2]. 

**Remedy:** Raise a purchase request on screen PUR-PR-01, obtain approval, and then raise a standard (STD) order against it [2][3].

*(Note: Under AMD-PUR-2026-03, which is not yet in force, the direct-order limit will change from £50,000 to £25,000 on 1 December 2026 [4].)*

When a UN 38.3 certificate is about to expire, the following procedure applies:

* **Monthly review:** On the first working day of each month, the senior buyer runs the certificate-expiry report (job JOB-PUR-022) using a 90-day window [1][2].
* **90 days before expiry:** The senior buyer writes to the supplier using letter template NBC-L-07 to request a new test report [1][2].
* **60 days before expiry:** If no new report has arrived, staff send a second reminder and notify the purchase manager [2][3]. Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, no new purchase orders may be placed once fewer than 60 days remain before expiry [1][3].
* **On expiry:** An email is sent to all buyers with the subject `CERT EXPIRED - DO NOT ORDER` alongside the supplier's name and code [3]. 

When received, renewed certificates must be uploaded onto a new row in Ledgerline ERP rather than overwriting existing records [3].

To raise a purchase request in Ledgerline ERP:

1. Open **PUR-PR-01**, enter the item code, and press **F3** (Fetch) to automatically populate the unit, warehouse, default cost centre, and estimated rate (based on the last released order) [2].
2. Verify your cost centre on **FIN-CC-01** before saving, as Ledgerline will not warn you if Finance has closed it [2].
3. Ensure the need-by date is today or later; a past date triggers ERR-PR-0105 [4].
4. Press **F8** to save the request in draft status (**DR**) [2][4]. Ledgerline calculates the estimated value assuming 20% VAT [4].
5. Press **F9** to submit [2][4]. If the estimated value is within your approval limit, it is approved immediately (**AP**); if it exceeds your limit, it moves to pending approval (**PA**) and routes to your manager [2][4].

Depending on your role and location:

Do not leave the area unattended or leave the pack on a workbench [2][4]. Raise the physical quarantine flag, notify your line supervisor, and apply an initial warning label [4].
- **Line supervisor:** Safely transfer the item to the outdoor fire-rated quarantine locker using protective gloves and a heavy-duty transit container (do not test, charge, or dismantle it) [4]. 
- **Stores:** Do not place the carton into fire cells; move it to quarantine with a red physical tag [1].
- **Ledgerline ERP:** Log the quarantine hold immediately after physical movement (via the quality engineer, or the shift supervisor if off-site) [4].

Depending on the document and context, **ERR-RMA-0211** has a few different meanings:

1. **Open claim/return exists**: A warranty claim or return record has already been logged and remains open against the serial number entered in `SERIAL NO` [1].
2. **Out of warranty**: When raised by `rma_approve`, the message is `OUT OF WARRANTY (<sold_dt>)`, caused because the rule 'out of warranty (<sold_dt>)' failed [2][4][5].
3. **Closing without receipt**: In the worked example for `rma_close`, it is raised if an operator attempts to close the return without receiving the goods [3].

Depending on the manual referenced, **ERR-WO-0310** has two documented meanings:

1. **Cancellation reason required**: Raised when attempting to cancel an order using the `wo_cancel` button without entering text into the `REASON` field [1].
2. **COMPONENT SHORTAGE (<itm_cd>)**: Raised by `wo_release` during work order release on `PRD-WO-01` when the rule 'component shortage (<itm_cd>)' fails because a raw material or sub-assembly line displays a deficit [2][3][4].

The sources define **ERR-PAY-0430** in two ways:

1. **RUN APPROVER SAME AS PROPOSER**: Occurs when an accounts payable clerk who creates or amends a payment proposal attempts self-approval (the rule 'run approver same as proposer' fails; raised by `pay_approve`) [1][2][3]. The approver cannot be the proposer; to resolve it, the user must log out so the accounts payable manager can log in with their own credentials to conduct the review [3][4].
2. **Payment file output directory inaccessible**: The system cannot write the electronic clearing file to the network drive during the `pay_file` service (resolved by checking network permissions and folder availability) [5].

Depending on the source consulted in Ledgerline ERP 7.2, `ERR-BNK-0101` has two definitions:

1. **BANK DETAILS NOT VERIFIED (<sup_cd>)**: The system rule 'bank details not verified (<sup_cd>)' failed [4][5]. Raised by `pay_approve` and `pay_file` [4], this error automatically excludes suppliers who have unverified or unconfirmed bank details/paperwork from the payment run [1][2]. The remedy is to correct the value shown and retry, or quote the code to the key user [4].
2. **Invalid bank account code**: In the Accounts Payable manual, it indicates that the entry in `BANK CD` does not match an active disbursement account in the general ledger master tables, or the selected account is marked as suspended for outgoing payments [3].

`ERR-CRD-0207` means "Credit limit exceeded" (`CREDIT LIMIT EXCEEDED (<cust_cd>)`) [1][4][5]. 

It indicates that the balance on the customer account, combined with the total value of unbilled orders including the current transaction, exceeds the credit limit authorised by finance [1]. 

When this occurs, the order cannot proceed or be confirmed until a payment is posted, credit clearance is obtained, or finance adjusts the customer's limit [1][3]. In Ledgerline ERP, this error is raised by the `so_confirm` service during order confirmation on screen `SAL-SO-01` [2][4][5].

To onboard a new supplier:

1. **Proposal**: A purchase executive or senior buyer proposes the supplier with at least one written quotation and the justification why existing suppliers cannot meet the need [1].
2. **Master Search**: Search the supplier master in Ledgerline (screen PUR-SUP-03) by name, city, and VAT number to verify an account does not already exist, and attach results to the file [1][4].
3. **Collect Documents**: Obtain the VAT registration certificate, company registration number, a bank letter confirming the account, proof of insurance, and the signed Supplier Code of Conduct [1].
4. **Approval & Creation**: The purchase manager approves the onboarding file [1]. Only after approval may the account be created in Ledgerline (screen PUR-SUP-01) [1]. 
5. **Orders**: No orders may be placed until all required documents (and lithium-cell certificates, if applicable) are on file [1].

The process normally takes five working days from a complete file [1][5].

To cancel a purchase order:

1. Check the receipt status of the order line before cancelling [3].
2. Press **Cancel** and enter a reason [1][2]. 
3. The order status updates to **CN**, committed budget is released, and if the order was released, the quantity is removed from stock on order [1].

To notify the supplier:
* Ledgerline does not send a cancellation notice [1][2]. 
* You must e-mail the supplier yourself on the same day to notify them in writing [2][3].
* Keep a copy of the sent e-mail filed directly against the order reference / order file, and archive electronic correspondence in the shared purchasing mailbox [2][5].

To upload a supplier certificate:

1. Select the correct supplier account in the Supplier master, go to the Certificates tab (service `sup_cert_upload`), and click **Add** [1][3].
2. Key the certificate type exactly as `UN38.3`, enter the document reference precisely as printed on the report, and enter the valid-to date [1][3].
3. Attach the legible scanned test report [1][3].
4. Press **F8** to save and verify that the status bar displays `CERT SAVED` [1][3].
5. Present form NBC-F-113 to the senior buyer to inspect alongside the on-screen record and initial [1][2].
6. Confirm the senior buyer has initialled NBC-F-113 before releasing any pending purchase orders, and file the form in the purchasing office compliance binder [2].

If the screen hangs after pressing Save:

- Do not press Save again, as doing so creates a second order [1].
- Wait one minute [1].
- Search for the order under Purchase, Order list by supplier, item, and today's date, or by client reference [1].
- If the order exists, the Save was successful; continue working from it [1].

To rescue an order stuck in Draft (DR) on a closed cost centre (warning W-CC-114) [1][4]:

1. Open the order on PUR-POM-06 and press Fetch [1][2].
2. Amend the cost centre to an open one [1][2].
3. Press F8 [2].

Ledgerline will recalculate the gross value, check the new cost centre, and commit the budget [2]. The order then becomes AP (approved) or PA (pending approval) by the normal rules [1][2]. Once approved, it can be released [2].

When a UN 38.3 certificate is approaching expiry:

- **90 days before expiry:** On the first working day of the month, the senior buyer identifies expiring certificates using report `JOB-PUR-022` (90-day window) and writes to the supplier using letter template `NBC-L-07` to request a new test report [1].
- **60 days before expiry:** If no report has arrived, a second reminder is sent and the purchase manager is notified [1]. Under amendment `AMD-SUP-2026-02`, no new order may be raised once fewer than 60 days remain [1].
- **On expiry:** An e-mail is sent to all buyers with the subject `CERT EXPIRED - DO NOT ORDER`, the supplier’s name, and code [1]. The supplier remains ACTIVE, but no lithium-cell parts may be ordered until a new certificate is uploaded and checked [3]. Because Ledgerline does not automatically stop orders, the person raising the order and the approver must enforce this check [3].

To receive goods against an order:

1. Confirm the order is released (status RL); unreleased orders are blocked with ERR-GRN-0102 [1][4].
2. Open screen INV-GRN-03, enter the purchase order number, and press Fetch [1][3].
3. Count the goods and enter the received quantity [1][3]. You cannot exceed the order balance (ERR-GRN-0204) [1][4].
4. Enter the supplier’s delivery note number in Remarks [1][3].
5. Press Save (or F8 Save) [1][3]. A part delivery receives its own GRN [1][3].

**W-CC-114** is a warning message displayed in Ledgerline ERP 7.2.3 when a purchase order is saved or submitted against a closed, retired, or dormant cost centre [1][2][4]. 

Instead of generating a hard failure and refusing the transaction, the system accepts the entry, generates a document reference, and sets the document status to Draft (displaying `DR` in the header block) with an amber confirmation banner [2][3]. 

The warning indicates that the order lines require cost centre amendment to an active account [1][2]. While held under W-CC-114, general ledger commitments are not posted, and printing, electronic transmission, and receipting functions remain locked until a valid cost centre is assigned and saved [2].

**ERR-SCR-0221** means **FETCH NOT DONE** [1][3][5]. 

It indicates that a purchase order on screen PUR-PO-01 was saved without running Fetch (F3) for the current supplier and item, or that the supplier or item was changed after Fetch was run [1][3][5]. Ledgerline rejects the save because the background linkages, supplier terms, and item data have not yet been retrieved [4][5]. 

It is raised by `po_save` [3][5]. The remedy is to press F3 (Fetch), verify the fetched values and details, and save again [1][3][5].

**ERR-APR-0009** means "No approver found" [1][3]. 

**Cause:** Nobody in the approver's management line has a limit that covers the document's value [1][3]. For example, Ledgerline shows this error for an order above £5,000,000, which exceeds the highest system limit [4]. It is raised by `pr_submit`, `po_save`, and `po_amend` [3].

**Remedy:** Follow your company's procedure for approvals above the highest limit in Ledgerline [1][3]. Documents above £5,000,000 require the Managing Director's written approval outside Ledgerline, which is then recorded by the plant head's office [4].

**ERR-SUP-0031** stands for **Supplier not active** [2][5]. 

It occurs because the supplier's status is **BLOCKED** [1][2][5]. Ledgerline refuses new orders to a blocked supplier (raised by `po_save`) [3][5]. 

To resolve it, use the supplier's active code; a blocked old code usually has a replacement [2][5]. Only the purchase manager may ask IT in writing to unblock a supplier [3].

`ERR-SUP-0118` means **VAT NO ALREADY REGISTERED** (or "VAT number already registered") [1][2][3]. 

- **Cause:** A supplier with this VAT number already exists in the system [1][3].
- **Raised by:** The `sup_create` service when attempting to create a supplier record [2][3][5]. Duplicates are refused by VAT number [5].
- **Remedy:** Search for the supplier and use the existing code; do not create a second record [1][3].

**ERR-PO-0610** (DIRECT PO LIMIT 50000 EXCEEDED, RAISE PR) means that a direct (DIR) purchase order cannot be saved because its gross value exceeds the direct-order limit [1][2][4]. 

Today, the limit is £50,000 [1][2][5]. 

**Remedy:** Raise a purchase request on PUR-PR-01, get it approved, and then raise a standard (STD) order against it [2][4].

*(Note: Under AMD-PUR-2026-03, which is not yet in force, the direct-order limit will decrease from £50,000 to £25,000 on 1 December 2026 [5].)*

**ERR-GRN-0204** means **QTY EXCEEDS PO BALANCE (\<qty>)** [3][4]. 

It is triggered during `grn_save` on screen INV-GRN-03 when an entered receipt quantity is greater than the purchase order's remaining balance (an over-delivery) [1][2][3][5]. 

When this occurs, halt the transaction [1]. You must either receive only the valid balance if instructed, or hold the entire delivery in the receiving bay while contacting purchasing; never adjust system figures to absorb extra stock [1]. The remedy is to correct the entered quantity and try again, or quote the code to the key user if the message persists [3].

**W-SUP-0207** is the advisory warning message **"UN38.3 CERTIFICATE MISSING OR EXPIRED"** in Ledgerline ERP [4][5]. 

Under patch 7.2.3-P4, it is designed to appear on purchase order entry screen `PUR-PO-01` when saving an order for an item flagged as a lithium cell if the supplier lacks an active UN38.3 certificate covering the order date (checking only the certificate's valid-to date) [5]. It does not stop the order from saving [2][5]. 

However, it is controlled by parameter `PUR.CERT_CHK` (default `N`), which the Change Advisory Board decided on 7 October 2026 to keep set to `N` until after the spring launch [2][5]. 

*(Note: In Ledgerline 7.3, planned for 1 March 2027, this warning will be replaced by the hard-stop error `ERR-SUP-0207` [1][3].)*

`ERR-RTV-0230` is the error message **"GRN ALREADY INVOICED, RAISE DEBIT NOTE"** [1][5].

The remedy is to have the user log out so the AP manager can log in with their own credentials to conduct the independent review [2]. It is raised by `pay_approve` [4].
2. **Payment file output directory inaccessible**: In the AP manual messages list, it indicates the system cannot write the electronic clearing file to the network drive during `pay_file` due to network permissions or folder issues [3].
3. **Ledgers locked for period closure**: In the AP manual worked example, it indicates the `pay_release` service stops because underlying ledgers are locked for period closure [5].

- **Duplicate Open Claim:** In MAN-SAL-72 § Messages, it indicates that a warranty claim or return record has already been logged and remains open against the serial number in `SERIAL NO` [3].
- **Goods Not Received:** In MAN-SAL-72 § Worked example, it is cited as being raised if an operator attempts to close the return (`rma_close`) without receiving the goods [1].

1. **COMPONENT SHORTAGE (<itm_cd>)**: Raised by `wo_release` during work order release on PRD-WO-01 when raw materials or sub-assemblies show a stock deficit or inadequate free stock [1][2][4][5]. 2. **Cancellation reason required**: Raised by `wo_cancel` if an operator attempts to cancel an order without entering text into the `REASON` field [3]. The remedy is to provide an explanation in the `REASON` field and press `wo_cancel` again [3].

2. **SAMPLE SIZE BELOW AQL PLAN:** In the error reference and service definition for `qin_post`, it indicates that the rule "sample size below aql plan" failed [3][4][5]. The remedy is to correct the value shown and try again, or quote the code to the key user if it persists [3].

**ERR-CRD-0207** indicates **Credit limit exceeded** [1][3]. 

This message means the balance on the customer account, combined with the total value of unbilled orders including the current transaction, exceeds the credit limit authorised by finance [1].

- The rule 'credit limit exceeded (`<cust_cd>`)' failed upon confirmation (`so_confirm`) [3][5].
- The sales order cannot be confirmed or proceed without credit clearance, which requires posting a payment or finance adjusting the customer's credit limit [1][4]. 

Remedy: correct the value shown and try again; if the message persists, quote the code to the key user [3].

To upload a supplier certificate in Ledgerline (service `sup_cert_upload`) [3][5]:

1. Open the Supplier master, go to the **Certificates** tab, and select **Add** [1][3].
2. Enter the certificate type exactly as **UN38.3**, key the document reference, and enter the valid-to date [1][3].
3. Attach the scanned test report [1][3].
4. Press **F8** to save; confirm the status bar displays **CERT SAVED** [1][3].
5. Present form **NBC-F-113** promptly for the senior buyer to inspect alongside the record and initial before releasing any pending purchase orders [1][2].
6. File the initialled **NBC-F-113** in the purchasing office compliance binder [2].

To onboard a new supplier, follow these steps:

1. **Search existing records**: Search the supplier master on screen PUR-SUP-03 by a distinctive name word, city, and VAT number; print and attach the result to the file [1][5].
2. **Raise request**: Complete form NBC-F-112 with at least one written quotation and an explanation of why existing suppliers cannot meet the need [1][5].
3. **Collect required documents**: Obtain the VAT registration certificate, company registration number, bank confirmation letter, proof of insurance, and signed Supplier Code of Conduct [1][5]. (For lithium-cell parts, obtain the UN 38.3 test report and summary) [5].
4. **Approval**: Obtain purchase manager approval via signature in box 7 of form NBC-F-112 before creating the account [1][5].
5. **Create record**: Create the supplier on screen PUR-SUP-01 (service `sup_create`) with name, city, country code, VAT number, and payment terms [1][5].

To rescue a Draft order stuck on a closed cost centre (warning W-CC-114):

1. Open the order on screen PUR-POM-06 and press Fetch [1].
2. Amend the cost centre to an open cost centre and press F8 [1][2][5]. 
3. Ledgerline recalculates the gross value, releases the committed budget, checks the new cost centre, and commits again [2].
4. The order then becomes AP (approved) or PA (pending approval) under normal rules [1][2]. 
5. Once approved, the order can be released [2].

If the screen hangs after pressing Save on an order:

- Do not press Save again, as pressing Save again creates a second order [1].
- Wait one minute [1].
- Search for the order under Purchase, Order list by supplier, item, and today's date, or by client reference [1].
- If the order exists, the Save worked, so you can continue from it [1].

To cancel a purchase order and notify the supplier:

1. Open the order on screen PUR-POM-06 and press Fetch [2]. Check the receipt status of the line before cancelling [3].
2. Press Cancel and enter a reason [1][2]. The order status becomes CN, committed budget is released, and for a released order, the quantity is removed from stock on order [1]. Orders in CN cannot be amended (ERR-PO-0801) [1][2].
3. Ledgerline does not send a cancellation notice automatically [1][2]. 
4. E-mail the supplier yourself on the same day with a written cancellation notice [2][3][4].
5. Keep the sent notification e-mail filed against the order reference [2][4]. Archive electronic correspondence in the shared purchasing mailbox and keep hard copies in the purchasing office [4].

To receive goods against a purchase order:

1. **Verify order status:** Check the delivery note against the PO [1]. The order must be in released status (`RL`); other statuses trigger `ERR-GRN-0102` [1][3].
2. **Open screen:** On `INV-GRN-03`, enter the PO number and press **Fetch** [1].
3. **Verify screen details:** Confirm the `RL` status, item description, unit of measure, and open balance [3].
4. **Enter counts:** Count the items physically and enter the verified floor count [1][3][4]. You cannot receive more than the remaining balance (error `ERR-GRN-0204`) [1][3].
5. **Set warehouse:** Lithium-cell parts must be received into quality hold warehouse `WH-MAN-QC` [1][3]. 
6. **Remarks:** Type the supplier's delivery note reference into **Remarks** [1][3].
7. **Save:** Press **Save** [1]. Note that partial deliveries require their own distinct GRN [1][2].

To raise a purchase request in Ledgerline:

1. Open screen **PUR-PR-01**, enter the item code, and press **F3** (Fetch) to retrieve item details [1]. Do not overwrite the description manually if the lookup fails [1].
2. Verify that the cost centre is marked as **OPEN** [1].
3. Enter the quantity in standard pack units and set a need-by date that allows for supplier lead periods (avoiding the current day) [1].
4. Press **F8** to save the record in draft status (**DR**) [1][2].
5. Press **F9** to submit, and check the status prompt at the foot of the screen [1][2]. 

If the requisition is within your personal spending limit, it is approved immediately; if it sits above your limit, it routes automatically to your manager [1][2].

When a UN 38.3 certificate is about to expire:

- **Within 90 days:** On the first working day of each month, the senior buyer runs the certificate-expiry report (job JOB-PUR-022) with a 90-day window [1]. For each expiring certificate, write to the supplier using letter template NBC-L-07 to request a new test report [1].
- **60 days before expiry:** If no new report has arrived, send a second reminder and inform the purchase manager [1]. Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, no new order may be raised once fewer than 60 days remain [1].
- **On expiry:** E-mail all buyers with the subject `CERT EXPIRED - DO NOT ORDER` and the supplier's name and code [1]. The supplier remains ACTIVE in the master, but an expired certificate counts as no certificate, and no lithium-cell parts may be ordered until a new certificate is uploaded and checked [3].

To raise an order after a purchase request is approved (status AP):

1. Open Purchase order entry (**PUR-PO-01**) [3][4].
2. Set the order type to **STD** and enter the request number in **Source PR** [3][4].
3. Enter the supplier and item code, then press **F3 (Fetch)** [3][4]. Fetch is mandatory; saving without it triggers error **ERR-SCR-0221** [3][4]. 
4. Check the tax code before saving: Fetch defaults to **VAT20-UK**; change it to **VAT20-RC** for suppliers outside the UK to prevent error **ERR-PO-0412** [4].
5. Press **F8** to save and check the **Status** field (**PA** means awaiting approval; **AP** means approved) [4].
6. Once in status AP, release the order on screen **PUR-POR-05** by pressing **F9** to reach status **RL** [4].

To return faulty goods to a supplier:

1. **Prerequisites**: Obtain the original GRN NO, ensure quality control has signed off the NCR NO for quality faults, verify collection is scheduled with the carrier, and confirm the receipt is not reversed [2].
2. **Physical Handling**: Move the goods to warehouse WH-MAN-RTV and label them clearly with the RTV number [5]. (Battery packs require approved crates with a UN3480 label via dangerous-goods freight [4][5]).
3. **Ledgerline Processing**: Within 30 days of receipt, raise the return to vendor (RTV) document on screen `INV-RTV-07` against the GRN [1][5]. 
4. **Invoiced Goods**: If the supplier's invoice is already posted, Ledgerline rejects the RTV with `ERR-RTV-0230` [1][3][5]. In this case, ask accounts payable to raise a debit note on screen `AP-DBN-04` instead [1][3][5].

1. **Do not update records yet:** Never accept bank changes by e-mail alone, nor amend the master file before verification [1][2][3]. If the e-mail is ambiguous, use `bnk_block` immediately to hold payments [4].
2. **Obtain formal written notice:** Secure confirmation on supplier stationery bearing an authorised signature [5].
3. **Conduct an independent call:** Two AP team members must participate on a call to a known contact [2][3]. Use contact numbers strictly from established ledger records, historical letterheads, or the supplier's public website—never from the e-mail or notice [1][2][3].
4. **Confirm details:** Verbally verify both existing and new account details [1]. If the contact cannot be reached or is unsure, place the account on temporary hold and alert Marta Kowalski immediately [1].
5. **Log verification:** Record the call on AP-BNK-06 (service `bnk_verify`) and staple the verification sheet to the original notice [2]. Submit for authorised verification once completed [1][4].

A damaged-pack incident is reported as follows:

* Once the pack is secured in the red quarantine bin in fire cell BAT-Z4, the team leader raises a non-conformance report to Quality on screen QA-NCR-02 during the same shift (before the shift ends) [1][2].
* The batch number stamped on the casing is entered into the system so Stores can freeze the remaining units from that intake pallet pending Quality inspection [2]. 
* Staff also log serial details in the quarantine register, complete the standard disposal notification, and file the paperwork in the department binder before updating the system [4].

When a pack is dropped, stop work immediately and do not leave it on a workbench [3][4][5]:

- **Immediate actions:** Under POL-BAT-004, leave the pack stationary, clear the gangway, and fetch the shift fire warden immediately [1]. Under SOP-QUA-002, raise the physical quarantine flag, apply an initial warning label, and notify the line supervisor without leaving the area unattended [5]. In stores, isolate dropped stock immediately regardless of appearance [2].
- **Physical transfer:** Under POL-BAT-004, carry it wearing heat-resistant gloves directly to the red quarantine bin in fire cell BAT-Z4, placing it flat and fully covered in vermiculite granules [3]. Under SOP-QUA-002, the line supervisor transfers it to the outdoor fire-rated quarantine locker using protective gloves and a heavy-duty transit container [5].
- **System logging:** The team leader logs a non-conformance report on screen QA-NCR-02 before shift end [3], and Quality applies a quarantine hold in Ledgerline ERP [5].

Screen AP-PAY-03 (*Accounts payable > Payment run*) processes supplier disbursements in sequential stages [3]:

1. **Setup**: Enter mandatory fields RUN DT, BANK CD, DUE UPTO, and optional SUP CD and COMMENT [2][3].
2. **Proposal**: Press `pay_propose` to run PAYMENT RUN PROPOSE, which evaluates eligible open items, assigns a RUN NO, and updates STATUS [2]. Items can be reviewed via `pay_get` or found with `pay_search` [2][4].
3. **Authorisation**: Submit the batch for approval by clicking `pay_approve` to invoke PAYMENT RUN APPROVE [1].
4. **Release**: A secondary authorised user clicks `pay_release` (PAYMENT RUN RELEASE) to lock the records and assign entries to the treasury release buffer [4].
5. **File Generation**: Press `pay_file` to execute PAYMENT RUN FILE, creating the bank transmission batch and posting entries to reduce supplier balances against the bank clearing control account [1][4].

If needed prior to release, proposals can be cancelled using `pay_cancel` with an explanation in REASON [1][4].

Under current policy POL-SUP-003 v2.3:

* **VAT number**: The VAT number is the definitive test of sameness; two records with the same VAT number are the same supplier [2]. In Ledgerline, saving a record with a duplicate VAT number fails with error `ERR-SUP-0118` [2][5].
* **Name and city match**: Suppliers may use short or varied names in communications. A name that is close to an existing supplier in the same city must be treated as that supplier until shown otherwise [2].
* **Different city or VAT number**: A near-match located in a different city or with a different VAT number is considered a different supplier [2].

To upload a supplier certificate:

1. Go to the Certificates tab of the supplier in Ledgerline [2][5].
2. Upload the certificate using service `sup_cert_upload` [1][2].
3. Provide the required fields [1][3]:
   - **Supplier Code (`sup_cd`)** [1]
   - **Certificate Type (`cert_type`)**: enter `UN38.3` for UN 38.3 certificates [1][2][5]
   - **Document Reference (`doc_ref`)**: ensure it matches the header on the scanned paperwork [1][3][5]
   - **Valid-To Date (`valid_to`)**: enter the correct expiry date [1][3][5]
4. Attach the scanned test report [2].

Before first ordering, ensure the details match the test report; the certificate must be checked by the senior buyer [7][8].

Under POL-SUP-003 v2.3, onboarding follows these steps:

1. **Proposal:** A purchase executive or senior buyer proposes the supplier with at least one written quotation and the reason an existing supplier cannot meet the need [2].
2. **Collect documents:** Before creation, collect the VAT registration certificate (VAT number), company registration number, a bank letter confirming the account, proof of insurance, and the signed Supplier Code of Conduct [2].
3. **Master search:** Search the supplier master on screen PUR-SUP-03 by name, city, and VAT number, and attach the search result to the onboarding file to check for duplicates [2].
4. **Approval and creation:** The purchase manager must approve the onboarding file [2]. Only after this approval may you create the supplier in Ledgerline on screen PUR-SUP-01 [2].

Suppliers must be onboarded and active before any purchase order can be placed [2][4].

If the screen hangs after you press Save:

- Do not press Save again, as doing so creates a second order [1].
- Wait one minute [1].
- Search for the order under Purchase, Order list using the supplier, item, and today's date, or search by client reference [1].
- If the order exists, the Save worked and you can continue from it [1].

To rescue an order stuck in Draft (DR) with warning W-CC-114 due to a closed cost centre:

1. Open the order on screen PUR-POM-06 and press Fetch [2].
2. Amend the cost centre to an open cost centre and press F8 [1][2][5][6]. (You can check whether a cost centre is open using screen FIN-CC-01 or by asking Finance [4].)

Once amended, Ledgerline checks the new cost centre and commits the budget again [6]. The order then moves to status AP or PA under normal rules, and can be released once approved [1][2].

To cancel a purchase order and notify the supplier:

1. Check the receipt status first; lines with processed delivery notes cannot simply be cancelled and must go through the standard returns routine [5].
2. Open the order on screen PUR-POM-06 [1][7].
3. Press Cancel and enter a reason [1][3]. 
4. The system changes the status to CN, releases the committed budget, and removes the quantity from stock on order if the order was released [3]. (Orders in status CN, RJ, or CL cannot be amended [1][3]).
5. Ledgerline does not send an automatic cancellation notice [1][3]. You must e-mail the supplier yourself in writing on the same day and keep a copy of the e-mail on the order file [1][2][3].

To receive goods against a purchase order:

1. Open screen **INV-GRN-03** via **Inventory > Goods receipt** [10].
2. Verify the supplier’s delivery note against the purchase order [1]. The order must be released (RL); unreleased orders will fail with error `ERR-GRN-0102` [1].
3. Enter the PO number and press **Fetch** [1][10].
4. Count the delivery physically before keying figures [2]. Enter the quantity received against each line [1][2]. You cannot exceed the outstanding balance (error `ERR-GRN-0204`) [1][3][10].
5. Record the supplier’s delivery note number (and any visible carrier damage) in **Remarks** for invoice matching [1][2][5].
6. If receiving lithium-cell parts, assign the destination warehouse to quality hold **WH-MAN-QC** [1][5].
7. Press **Save** (or **F8 Save**) [1][2][10]. 

A separate GRN must be created for each partial delivery [1][2][3][10].

When a UN 38.3 certificate is about to expire:

1. **90 days before expiry:** On the first working day of each month, the senior buyer runs the certificate-expiry report (JOB-PUR-022) with a 90-day window and writes to the supplier using letter template NBC-L-07 to request a new test report [1][3].
2. **60 days before expiry:** If no new report has arrived, a second reminder is sent and the purchase manager is informed [1]. Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, no new purchase orders may be raised once fewer than 60 days remain [1].
3. **On expiry:** An email is sent to all buyers with the subject `CERT EXPIRED - DO NOT ORDER`, including the supplier's name and code [1]. 

Renewed certificates must be uploaded to Ledgerline ERP on a new row and never overwrite the previous record [1][4].

To raise a purchase request in Ledgerline ERP:

1. If a new supplier is needed, clear it through the accounts office before entering a requisition [1].
2. Go to screen **PUR-PR-01** [3].
3. Enter the item code and press **F3** (Fetch) [3]. Ledgerline fills the unit, warehouse, default cost centre, and an estimated rate based on the last released order for the item [3].
4. Check the cost centre on **FIN-CC-01** before saving, as Ledgerline does not warn you if your default cost centre has been closed by Finance [3].
5. Press **F8** to save (status **DR**) [3].
6. Press **F9** to submit [3]. 

A request within your approval limit is approved immediately (status **AP**); a request above your limit is sent to your manager [2][3].

To return faulty goods to a supplier:

1. **Physical segregation:** Immediately move rejected items to the quarantine area (warehouse WH-MAN-RTV) and label them clearly with the return identifier [4][5][7][10].
2. **Pre-checks:** Locate the original GRN NO, ensure quality control has signed off the NCR NO, and confirm purchasing has scheduled carrier collection [4].
3. **System processing:**
   - If the invoice is unposted, raise a Return to Vendor (RTV) document on screen INV-RTV-07 within 30 days of receipt [1][10].
   - If the invoice has already been posted, INV-RTV-07 will halt with error ERR-RTV-0230; pass the purchase order reference and quarantine docket to purchase ledger to raise a debit note on screen AP-DBN-04 [2][9][10].
4. **Dispatch:** Ensure system-generated paperwork accompanies the freight and retain the carrier’s signed collection manifest [2][5][10].

If a battery pack is dropped:

1. **Halt work and secure the area:** Leave the pack stationary, clear the gangway, and fetch the shift fire warden immediately [1][4]. Do not leave it unattended or on a workbench [3][4][5].
2. **Flag and notify:** Raise the physical quarantine flag, apply an initial warning label/tag, and notify the line supervisor [4][6]. It must be isolated and quarantined regardless of external appearance [2][8].
3. **Safe transfer:** The line supervisor arranges transfer using protective gloves and a heavy-duty transit container to the designated outdoor fire-rated quarantine locker, without attempting to test, charge, or dismantle it [4]. Alternatively, move it immediately to the red quarantine bin in fire cell BAT-Z4 and cover it with vermiculite; never place it in standard scrap cages [5][7].
4. **Log the issue:** Report it to Quality within the same shift using screen QA-NCR-02 [5][7].

When a request is approved (status AP), raise the order on screen PUR-PO-01 [4]:

1. Set the order type to STD and enter the approved request number in **Source PR** [4][6].
2. Enter the supplier and the item [4][6].
3. Press **F3 (Fetch)** before saving [4][6]. Fetch populates the rate, tax code, payment terms, warehouse, cost centre, need-by date, and quantity directly from the request [6].

Fetch is mandatory; Ledgerline 7.2.3 will refuse to save the order and display `ERR-SCR-0221 (FETCH NOT DONE)` if Fetch is not run for the current supplier and item [6][9] (superseding older procedure where Fetch was optional [3]). If you alter the supplier or item after fetching, press F3 again before saving [6].

The payment run operates in Ledgerline ERP 7.2 as follows:
1. **Proposal**: Click `pay_propose` to call PAYMENT RUN PROPOSE (proposal job JOB-AP-030), generating a draft register and RUN NO [5][9].

5. **File Generation**: Click `pay_file` to run PAYMENT RUN FILE (JOB-AP-031) to create the bank export file, and email remittances [1][7][8].

To put battery cartons away:

1. Move incoming deliveries into the battery store immediately; never leave them on the general receiving dock [6].
2. Inspect packaging seals and outer casings for puncture, crushing, moisture, or drop damage before moving stock; never place suspect, damaged, or dropped cartons into fire cells—quarantine them immediately [1][3][6].

4. Put packs away only in fire cells BAT-Z1 to BAT-Z4 [1].

Under current policy, determine whether two records are the same supplier using the following rules:

- **VAT number:** The VAT number is the test of sameness; two records with the same VAT number are the same supplier [2]. Ledgerline blocks creating a second supplier with a registered VAT number with error ERR-SUP-0118 [2].
- **City and name matching:** A name close to an existing supplier in the same city must be treated as that supplier until shown otherwise [2].
- **Different city or VAT number:** A near-match in a different city or with a different VAT number is a different supplier [2].

An overseas supplier must be processed under the reverse charge mechanism using a tax code ending in `-RC` [2][7][8]. 

For standard orders, the default code `VAT20-UK` must be amended to `VAT20-RC` (VAT 20%, reverse charge) to avoid error `ERR-PO-0412` [1][3][4][5][7]. Depending on the applicable rate, active reverse charge codes for overseas suppliers are:
- `VAT20-RC` (20%) [5]
- `VAT5-RC` (5%) [5]
- `VAT0-RC` (0% / zero-rated) [6]

The service `sup_create` uses screen PUR-SUP-01 (SUPPLIER MASTER CREATE) [1][3][6][8].
The `state` field of a supplier represents the two-letter country code (COUNTRY CD (2), 1998 name) [3][4]. It is a required text field [3][4].

`fetch_tok` is a temporary validation token returned by the Fetch service (`po_fetch`) and required by Save (`po_save`) [1][3][6]. It is valid once, for a single supplier and item or part reference [1][2][6]. 

On screen PUR-PO-01, it appears as a hidden string field [9]. For automated interfaces and external data routines, `po_fetch` must be called before `po_save`, and `fetch_tok` must be passed as a mandatory parameter in the `po_save` payload [4][6][7]. If the token is omitted, invalidated, or does not match the active supplier and part reference, the payload is rejected [6]. 

In the database, it is defined in the `fetch_tok` table under the `PUR/core` module, with fields including `tok` (primary key), `user_id`, `screen`, `ctx`, `created_on`, and `used` [5][8].

For a duplicate, `sup_create` raises `ERR-SUP-0118` (VAT NO ALREADY REGISTERED) [1][4][10]. 

Duplicates are refused only by exact VAT number; a supplier entered without a VAT number is never checked [1][2].

**Remedy:**

To raise a purchase request under SOP-PUR-002 v1.4 [3]:

1. Open screen PUR-PR-01 [3].
2. Enter the item code and press F3 (Fetch) [3]. Ledgerline automatically populates the unit, warehouse, your default cost centre, and an estimated rate based on the last released order [3].
3. Check the cost centre on screen FIN-CC-01 before saving, because Ledgerline does not warn you on the request if Finance has closed your default cost centre [3].
4. Press F8 to save the request in draft status (DR) [3].
5. Press F9 to submit the request [3]. If it is within your limit, it is approved immediately; otherwise, it is routed to your manager [3].

When a UN 38.3 certificate is about to expire:

- If no new report arrives by 60 days before expiry, a second reminder is sent and the purchase manager is notified [5]. 
- Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, no new order may be raised once fewer than 60 days remain [5].
- Upon expiry, an e-mail with the subject "CERT EXPIRED - DO NOT ORDER" and the supplier's name and code is sent to all buyers [5]. No lithium-cell part may be ordered until a new certificate is uploaded and checked [3].

W-CC-114 is a warning message issued when a purchase order is saved or amended against a closed, dormant, or retired cost centre [1][2][5]. 

Under Ledgerline ERP 7.2.3, rather than causing a hard failure or refusal, the system accepts the entry but sets or reverts the order status to Draft (`DR`) with an amber confirmation banner [1][2][3][4]. The order reference is generated, but general ledger commitments, printing, electronic transmission, and receipting functions remain locked until the cost centre is reassigned to an active account and saved afresh [2][5].

**ERR-SCR-0221** corresponds to the error message **FETCH NOT DONE** [4][5]. 

It occurs when an order on screen **PUR-PO-01** is saved without running Fetch for the active supplier and item combination, or after modifying them [1][3][4]. Ledgerline requires this retrieval step to verify supplier terms and item details before saving to the database [3]. 

**Remedy:**
* **Manual entry:** Press **F3** (Fetch), verify the fetched details, and press Save again [1][3][4].
* **Integrations:** Call `po_fetch` prior to `po_save` and pass the returned validation token `fetch_tok` [3].

ERR-SUP-0031 means "SUPPLIER NOT ACTIVE" in the SUP module [1][4][5]. It occurs because the supplier's status is BLOCKED [2][3].

**ERR-PO-0610** means that a DIR (direct) order's gross value exceeds the direct-order limit [5].

**ERR-SUP-0118** corresponds to the message **VAT NO ALREADY REGISTERED** [2][3][4][5]. 

It is raised by the `sup_create` service when attempting to register a supplier with a VAT number that already exists in the system [1][5]. 

The remedy is to search for the existing supplier and use that code rather than creating a duplicate record [5]. Duplicates are refused only by VAT number; suppliers entered without one are not checked [1].

On screen AP-PAY-03 (Accounts payable > Payment run), the payment run operates through sequential steps [2][5]:

1. **Parameters**: Enter mandatory fields `RUN DT`, `BANK CD`, `DUE UPTO`, and optional fields `SUP CD` and `COMMENT` [2][5].
2. **Compile proposal**: Click `pay_propose` to call PAYMENT RUN PROPOSE, which creates the draft proposal and assigns a `RUN NO` [5].
3. **Review**: Click `pay_get` to retrieve proposed transactions into the working grid to inspect vouchers and exclude items if needed [5].
4. **Approve**: An authorised user clicks `pay_approve` to run PAYMENT RUN APPROVE [1][5].
5. **Release**: A secondary authorised user reviews the approved run and clicks `pay_release` (PAYMENT RUN RELEASE) to assign entries to the treasury release buffer [1][3].
6. **Generate bank file**: Click `pay_file` (PAYMENT RUN FILE) to export the transmission batch to the bank interface directory and post general ledger updates [1][3].

3. Check the tax code: Fetch defaults to **VAT20-UK**; change it to **VAT20-RC** for suppliers outside the UK to prevent error **ERR-PO-0412** [2].

5. Release an approved order (**AP**) on screen **PUR-POR-05** using **F9**; the order reaches the supplier only when in status **RL** [2].

No [1][3]. Under POL-SUP-003 v2.3 and Purchase Policy 6.2, a valid UN 38.3 certificate must be uploaded in Ledgerline against the supplier and checked before the first order is placed [1][3]. 

No lithium-cell part may be ordered until the certificate is uploaded and verified [1][3]. Although Ledgerline ERP does not automatically block an order without a certificate, the check must be carried out by the person raising the order and by the approver before ordering [1][3]. Additionally, under AMD-SUP-2026-02, the test report must be less than 12 months old and remain valid for at least 60 days after the order [1][5].

Yes, Ledgerline 7.3 will block orders for lithium-cell items with error ERR-SUP-0207 if the supplier lacks a valid UN38.3 certificate [1][2]. 

However, this is not yet in place today [1]. Ledgerline 7.3 is not scheduled to take effect until 1 March 2027 [1]. Currently, Ledgerline does not stop an order to a supplier without a certificate [4]; version 7.2.3-P4 only displays warning W-SUP-0207 [1][2], and compliance checks must be manually carried out by the person raising the order and by the approver [4].

No, chargers did not always need a UN 38.3 certificate [4][5]. 

Under earlier policy (POL-PUR-001 v3.0), only battery packs required a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate, while hub motors and chargers were explicitly not covered [4]. 

Under the current policy (POL-PUR-001 v4.1, § 6.2 and POL-SUP-003 v2.3, § 4.1), chargers are classified as lithium-cell parts alongside battery packs, hub motors, and any item marked lithium-cell in the item master, and they may only be bought from a supplier holding a valid UN 38.3 certificate [2][5].

In Ledgerline ERP 7.2, approval limits are stored directly on the individual user record itself, entirely outside the role table [1][3][5]. 

Approval limits previously sat within general role definitions, but moved from roles to user records [5]. A user's assigned role governs their available screens, menus, and background services, whereas their financial approval limit is set directly on their user profile from the company's approval matrix [1][3][5].

Under the 2019 policy (POL-PUR-001 v3.0), a direct purchase order without a request was permitted only when its gross value, including VAT, was £30,000 or less [1][2].

Please note that v3.0 is superseded [1][2]. On 2025-04-01, version 4.0 increased the direct-order limit to £50,000 or less, including VAT [3][4]. This remains the rule in force under the current policy, POL-PUR-001 v4.1 [4].

The tax code for standard-rate VAT (20%) on a UK supplier is VAT20-UK [2][4], in line with the requirement that UK suppliers are charged standard UK VAT using codes ending in -UK [3]. This has been in force since the standard rate changed to 20% on 4 January 2011 [2].

Under superseded guidance, V1 was the tax code for standard-rate VAT at 17.5%, applied on purchase orders for standard components, tooling, carriage, and workshop consumables [1].

Under the policy in force today (POL-TEX-007 v2.4), you have 60 days from the expense to enter a claim on screen AP-EXP-09 [2][5]. 

From 1 January 2027, under POL-TEX-007 v3.0, this submission window will reduce to 45 days [1][5].
